chunks.text: M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 IN THE COURT OF SH. SUNIL BENIWAL, DISTRICT JUDGE-06, SOUTH DISTRICT, SAKET COURTS, NEW DELHI. CS DJ 222/2023 CNR No. DLST010038212023 M/s Chandra Associates Pvt. Ltd., Regd. Office at: A-15A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi, Through its Director Ms. Poonam Singhal .....PLAINTIFF VERSUS Sh. Arun Chopra E-84, First Floor, Greater Kailash-2, New Delhi 110 048. .....DEFENDANT Date of Institution : 21.04.2023 Date of conclusion of Arguments : 17.01.2026 Date of Judgment : 27.02.2026 SUIT FOR RECOVERY OF RS. 38,00,728/- JUDGMENT Plaintiff has filed the present suit against the defendant for recovery of Rs. 38,00,728/- along with pendente-lite and future interest @ 12% per annum from the date of filing of the present suit till the realization of the said amount. In brief, the case of the plaintiff is that It is averred that the plaintiff is a company duly incorporated under the Companies Act, 1956 and is having its registered office at A-15A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi wherein Ms. Poonam Singhal is one of the Directors of the Plaintiff Company and is duly authorised and empowered to sign, verify and institute the present suit for an on behalf of the Company, by virtue of the Board Resolution dated 2023, passed by the Board of Directors of the Plaintiff Company, in its meeting held at the M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 registered office of the Company.

It is further averred that the Plaintiff is the absolute owner and in possession of the property bearing No. A-15A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi. The Defendant has been residing in a portion of the aforesaid property i.e. on the first floor of the said property alongwith terrace. When the Plaintiff purchased the aforesaid property from its erstwhile owner, the Defendant was in illegal and unauthorised occupation of the suit property as a sub-tenant. The Plaintiff, pursuant to purchase of the aforesaid property, requested the Defendant to vacate the suit property, however, the defendant refused to vacate the same. Upon the failure of the Defendant to vacate the suit property, the Plaintiff was constrained to institute an eviction petition against Smt. Krishna Gupta and the Defendant. It is further averred that the said eviction petition bearing RC No. 6087/2016 was allowed by the court of Sh. Sachin Sangwan, the then ARC/CC)/AC), vide order dated 25.09.2019 but despite the aforesaid eviction orders, the Defendant failed, neglected and refuted to vacate the aforesaid property/portion of the Plaintiff and thereafter, filed an absolutely false, frivolous and misconceived Appeal, which was also dismissed by the Ld. Court of Sh. Narottam Kaushal, DJ (South), Saket Courts, New Delhi, vide order dated 07.05.2022.

It is further averred that the Plaintiff, in order to get possession of the suit property, filed execution Application before the court of Ld. RC, South, Saket Courts, New Delhi. The Defendant, with the ulterior and oblique motives, filed frivolous and vexatious objections in the same and further delayed the execution. Ultimately, when the said objections were dismissed by the Hon'ble Court, the Defendant, on 10.02.2023, surrendered the possession of the suit property by handing over the keys of the property to the AR of the Plaintiff, before the Ld. Executing Court. It is further averred that after receipt of keys of the property, the AR of the property opened the locks of the property and inspected the property and upon inspection of the property, it was observed that the property was in dilapidated condition in as much as the Defendant had already vacated the property long back and had shifted to E-B4, First Floor, Greater Kailash-2, New Delhi, along with his family. The Defendant had not been maintaining the property and was not even getting the minor repair and maintenance work done in respect of the property, which led to the property to be in the aforesaid miserable state. After getting possession of the property, the Plaintiff got the said property checked and inspected from an architect in order to ascertain the damages to the property and estimate of the repair works, which would be required to make the suit property habitable. It is further averred that the said architect thoroughly inspected the entire property, took photographs of the same and gave his detailed report dated 04.03.2023, as per which, an amount of Rs. 9.00 to Rs. 10.00 lacs would be required for repair, maintenance and other expenses, whereafter, the suit property may be made habitable.

It is further averred that though the Defendant had been occupying the aforesaid portion/property as an illegal sub-tenant and unauthorised occupant, however, since the date of M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 passing of the aforesaid eviction orders, his status in the aforesaid tenanted premises as that of illegal and unauthorised occupant has been affirmed by the Court. Even the appeal filed by the Defendant against the said order had been dismissed by the Ld. DJ (South), Saket Courts, New Delhi. The Defendant handed over the actual and vacant possession of the suit property to the Plaintiff on 10.02.2023. It is further averred that it is trite in law that a person/tenant/sub-tenant, who remains in unauthorised and illegal possession of the property, after passing of order eviction against him, is liable to pay market rent to the owner/landlord, w.e.f. passing of order of eviction till the date of handing over the possession of the property. The market rent for such like property in the vicinity of the aforesaid portion/property is not less than Rs. 75,000/- per month. Since the Defendant has been occupying the suit property as an illegal and unauthorised occupant, the Plaintiff is entitled to a sum of Rs. 75,000/- per month from him, on account of your illegal occupation of the aforesaid property/portion, being the market rent of similarly placed/situated property in the aforesaid locality.

It is averred that the defendant is liable to pay a sum of Rs. 75,000/- per month to the Plaintiff for three years preceding the filing of the suit i.e. from March, 2020 till February, 2023 when the actual and vacant physical possession of the property was handed over by the Defendant to the Plaintiff. Besides the aforesaid, the Defendant is also liable to pay a sum of Rs. 10.00 lacs towards the expenses, which would be incurred by the Plaintiff in order to make the suit property re-habitable and re-usable. Further a sum of Rs. 1,00,728/- is due and payable by the Defendant towards water bill/user charges payable to the authorities concerned. Accordingly, it is averred that the Plaintiff is entitled to the following amount: User charges from March, 2020 till February, 2023 : Rs. 27.00 lacs Expenses to be incurred by the Plaintiff as per report of Architect : Rs. 10.00 lacs Unpaid water bill : Rs. 1,00,728/- TOTAL : Rs. 38,00,728/-

It is further averred that the Plaintiff is also entitled to interest on the aforesaid amount from the date of filing of the suit till actual realisation of the aforesaid amount, @ 12% p.a., which is prevalent rate of interest on such like transactions. Plaintiff, after passing the order of eviction by the Ld. Trial Court, caused a legal notice dated 16.12.2020, to the Defendant, calling upon the defendant to pay user charges of the suit property at the prevailing market rate, as the defendant had been in illegal and unauthorised occupation of the suit property after passing of eviction order by the Ld. Trial Court. The defendant received the said notice, but failed to pay the user charges for his illegal and unauthorised occupation of the suit property. The defendant replied to the said notice, by sending a false, frivolous and misconceived reply. That in view of the aforesaid, it is submitted that the Plaintiff is entitled to a sum of Rs. 37.00 lacs from the Defendant, the details whereof, are mentioned in para 20 of the plaint. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 Accordingly, plaintiffs prayed for recovery of total amount of Rs. 38,00,728/- along with pendente lite and future interest @ 12% per annum from the date of present suit till the repayment of said friendly loan. Hence, the present suit.

Summons of suit were served on the defendant who filed the written statement wherein preliminary objections were taken that there is no privity of contract of the plaintiff with defendant as such the suit itself is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed for this ground alone; that suit is bad for non joinder of necessary party to which the plaintiff is claiming to be its tenant i.e. Krishna Gupta who is deceased now but her legal representative are necessary and proper party for adjudication of the present case; the suit is bad for non joinder of necessary party; the suit is not maintainable for misrepresentation, concealment and suppression of material facts and plaintiff is not entitled to any relief; there is no cause of action to file the present suit against the defendant and is liable to be rejected under order 7 Rule 11 CPC.

It is contended that during pendency of eviction petition the alleged Director of the Plaintiff Company filed evidence on behalf of the Plaintiff Company based on incorrect facts which are contrary to pleadings in the pending suit before Hon'ble High Court in CS (OS) No. 2075/2007. The said suit has been filed by the purchaser to whom the Plaintiff Company has sold the suit property during pendency of eviction proceedings. Therefore, the purchaser is a necessary party to the present proceedings in view of the pleadings before the Hon'ble High Court in the said suit. In the said suit the Plaintiff Company has vide order dated 11.02.2019 shown its ignorance about the eviction proceedings against the Defendant. Plaintiff has obtained the eviction order by playing fraud on the Court in those proceedings but in the present proceedings in view of pleadings in CS (OS) 2075/2007 the Plaintiff in the said suit is a necessary party for adjudication of the present case. It is further stated that during pendency of proceedings inter se the parties in eviction proceedings, Mr. Manoj Singhal claimed himself to be representative of the Plaintiff Company without title sold the property to Mr. Vinod Gupta who has filed a suit for specific performance before Hon'ble High Court. In the said proceedings the Plaintiff Company has denied filing any eviction proceedings as well as given any authority to Mr. Manoj Singhal to deal with the suit property in any manner. As such in view of contradictory stand on record on affidavit before various Courts the present suit is liable to be dismissed for abusing the process of the Hon'ble Court.

In the preliminary objections, it is averred that the property A 15A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi was purchased in the name of Dr Ramesh Gupta through his attorney Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta who was elder brother of Dr Ramesh Gupta. Dr Ramesh Gupta executed a registered General Power of Attorney dated 26.08.1976 and authorised his elder brother Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta to induct tenant. The defendant was inducted as a tenant on 21st May 1981 by Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta being the attorney of Dr Ramesh Gupta. Dr Ramesh Gupta visited India three-four M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 times but neither written agreement was executed nor were any proper rent receipts issued. Dr Ramesh Gupta was receiving rent regularly from the defendant through his representative Mrs Krishna Gupta who was none but the wife of his elder brother Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta who had purchased the property on behalf of Dr Ramesh Gupta as his power of attorney holder.

It is further averred that since Dr Ramesh Gupta was owner of the property and Mr Tarsem Prakash Gupta being his brother was his attorney and rent was being received by Krishna Gupta, wife of Tarsem Prakash Gupta and Bhabhi of Dr Ramesh Gupta, therefore, the defendant filed a suit for declaration against all the three to declare him a tenant in the premises A-15A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi. The tenancy of the defendant was well within the knowledge of all the three since 1981 and by way of suit brought to the knowledge in 1983 also. After filing of the suit, a Lease Agreement dated 05.08.1983 was executed by Late Mrs. Krishna Gupta wife of attorney in favour of the defendant duly witnessed by the Attorney of Dr. Ramesh Gupta. This fact is admitted by the witness of the Plaintiff Company in his evidence. This lease agreement has been duly accepted in all proceedings by the parties.

It is further averred that suddenly certain persons started claiming to have purchased the property bearing no. A 15 A, Hauz Khas, New Delhi. The Defendant never received any communication from Dr Ramesh Gupta or his attorney to this effect and defendant continued to pay rent as usual. The defendant filed a petition for fixation of standard rent for the suit premises because the family members Dr Ramesh Gupta, Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta and Smt. Krishna Gupta started harassing to increase the rent. In the said petition all the three family members were arrayed as party, Dr Ramesh Gupta, Shri Tarsem Prakash Gupta and Krishna Gupta. In the pleadings of the said case which was never heard and adjudicated, the subsequent purchaser, the plaintiff in collusion with Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Prakash Gupta conspired to commit forgeries and fabrication to evict the defendant from the premises and filed forged vakalatnama and written statement on behalf of Dr Ramesh Gupta. Copy of pleadings of the said case and without proof marked as Exhibit P6, 7 & 8 in the eviction proceedings and made the basis for deciding the rent case.

It is further averred that the pleadings and averments by the LRs of Late Mrs. Krishna Gupta in the eviction case ruled out the possibility of any relationship of landlord and tenant between Ramesh Gupta and Krishna Gupta on the basis of following facts: € Property in question was purchased by HUF Sh Shiv Chand Ramesh Kumar. To prove this Shri Tarsem Prakash placed on record assessment orders of Income Tax and Wealth Tax. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 € Ramesh Gupta with a view to defraud the HUF and its other members executed a sale deed in favour of Chandra Associates at a throw away price in order to avoid payment of income tax and to obtain clearance from the income tax authorities, he manipulated the fact and shown Krishna Gupta his real 'Bhabhi' as one of the tenants in the property. He had also shown Shri Thakur Das his real 'Jija' as a tenant in the property whereas the fact is that Shri Thakur Das never resided in the said house. € Chandra Associates has not acquired perfect title of the property but on his own assuming themselves to be the landlord had filed the eviction petition against late Smt Krishna Gupta the real Bhabhi of Ramesh Gupta. Since in the sale deed she was shown as tenant so 'assumed' landlord conveniently made a ground of sub-letting/assigning or otherwise parting with the possession of the premises in favour of the defendant whereas the fact is that Arun Chopra was inducted by HUF itself and even from the property is shown in the name of HUF in the income tax records. So there was no question of sub-letting. € The LRs of late Smt Krishna Gupta denied any admission made in standard rent proceedings by Smt Krishna Gupta. The alleged written statement filed by Smt Krishna Gupta and Tarsem Gupta have not been put for admission or denial either to Smt Krishna Gupta or to her successor. There is no question of any admission of the same unless the document is put for admission or denial on records.

It is further averred that Late Mrs. Krishna Gupta and her husband who was the brother of Ramesh Gupta submitted before Income Tax Department in their reply to notice wherein they admitted that the defendant is a tenant of Dr Ramesh Gupta. From the documents placed on record by the LRs of the deceased Mrs. Krishna Gupta in the nature of Assessment Order of Income Tax Department and Wealth Tax Department of the Assessment Year 1968-69 which are more than 30 years old document the family of the Late Mrs. Krishna Gupta was initially a bigger HUF firm of M/S Raja Ram Shiv Chand. Raja Ram was the brother of Shiv Chand. It was partitioned. Then it consisted of M/S Shiv Chand Ramesh Chand of which Shri Shiv Chand the father of Ramesh and Tarsem and father in law of Krishna was the Karta.

It is further averred that vide Assessment Order of the year 1968-69, 1969-70, 1970-71, 1971-72 placed on record by LRs of late Mrs. Krishna Gupta in reply to an application under order 12 rule 6 in eviction proceedings as well as one of the LR Mr. Pawan Gupta has filed his evidence and relied on these documents which are more than 30 years old document issued by Wealth Tax Department and Income Tax Department. In the said statutory documents which are more than 30 years old the property in question and income derived from the property is shown HUF property of M/S Shiv Chand Ramesh Kumar having address of A-15 A Hauz Khas, New Delhi. Since Mrs Krishna Gupta was proceeded ex-parte in the eviction proceedings because she was not served at her latest whereabouts as such LRs were not allowed to tender their evidence. Hence these documents were not proved in the eviction proceedings which was decided merely on the basis of self-created documents by the Plaintiff filed in earlier cases and those cases were never adjudicated nor were the documents or pleadings proved which was the basis of adjudication of eviction proceedings. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026

It is further averred that after purchase of the property, in the statutory documents which are more than 30 years old, i.e. Assessment order of Wealth Tax and Income Tax of the firm Shiv Charan Ramesh Kumar HUF reflects the purchase of the property and income from the property as that of income of HUF and the ownership of the property by HUF. As such Tarsem Gupta and other family of HUF were the owners of the property. The ld. Courts in eviction proceedings has allowed the petition merely on the contents of the document (not proved), on the ground that in the sale deed original owner has stated in para 6 that the first floor was occupied by two tenants, viz. Krishna Gupta and Thakur Dass Gupta. It is pertinent to mention that Krishna Gupta is the bhabhi of Ramesh Gupta who was living on the ground floor with the family and TD Gupta is the brother in law (sister's husband) of Ramesh Gupta and was the resident of X-13, Green Park, New Delhi, the said address is already mentioned in the Sale Deed in as much as he was shown as one of the witness. It is pertinent to mention that neither Ramesh Gupta nor his attorney Tarsem Parkash nor his wife Krishna Gupta has ever filed any case against the defendant nor Ramesh Gupta has filed any case against his bhabhi Krishna Gupta as stated in the contents of Sale Deed.

It is further averred that the in reply of the LRs of late Smt Krishna Gupta as well as reply before Income Tax authorities where it is categorically stated that the defendant is not a sub tenant. He is a direct tenant. Ld. Courts in eviction proceedings failed to adjudicate on locus of the plaintiff to file case through its alleged Directors by ignoring the facts that in April 1995 the Plaintiff M/S Chandra Associates filed a case through Mr. Vinod Singhal under Section 14(1) (b) of the Delhi Rent Control Act, 1958. It is pertinent to mention that Mr. Vinod Singhal was the alleged owner of 150 sq yds of A-15 A Hauz Khas and not this portion of 350 sq yds. There is no whisper in the entire petition about authorisation of Mr. Vinod Singhal to file the petition when he was not the owner of the suit property. Mr. Vinod Singhal did not tender his evidence. It is further averred that thereafter one Mr. Manoj Singhal claimed himself to be Director of the Plaintiff Company. On record no Form 32 was filed by Mr. Manoj Singhal in the capacity as Director of the Plaintiff Company as well as there was no Resolution dated 06.07.2008 as mentioned in his affidavit of evidence authorizing Mr. Manoj Singhal to tender evidence on behalf of the Plaintiff Company. In view of these facts the evidence of Mr. Manoj Singhal could not be relied on. But since the Defendant was also keen to hand over the keys of the property to the rightful owner in view of poor condition of the building which was not in a habitable position.

It is further averred that it is pertinent to mention that during the pendency of the case Mr. Manoj Singhal had also entered into an Agreement to sell dated 08.11.2006 with one Mr. Vinod Gupta in respect of entire property measuring 500 sq yds. without any authorisation. Pleadings of the said suit was also filed on ARC record. Vide said pleadings Mr. Manoj Singhal has categorically accepted that he was not the Director of the Plaintiff company. But entire eviction proceedings were decided on the basis of evidence of Mr. Manoj Singhal who had played fraud with the Hon'ble Court in both the proceedings, i.e in eviction proceedings and in civil suit pending before Hon'ble High Court. Present suit has been filed through Ms Poonam Singhal without disclosing the fact that when did she became Director of the Plaintiff Company. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 It is further averred that in the said CS(OS)2075/2007 the witness/one of the defendant Mr. Manoj Singhal in cross examination has deposed that the total property is 500 sq yds out of which 350 sq yds is owned by defendant no. 2 (M/S Chandra Associates) and 150 sq yds is owned by defendant no. 1 (Mr. Manoj Singhal) and 3 in the said suit. In the testimonials/statement dated

2017 Mr. Manoj Singhal has accepted that no Resolution was passed by the Company in his favour to deal with the property. In the said suit the Plaintiff Company has filed its written statement on 14.12.2007 and stated categorically on affidavit that Mr. Manoj Singhal has no authority to transfer the property bearing No. A-15A, Hauz Khas, measuring 500 sq yds. as he is not the exclusive/absolute owner thereof. It is further stated by the Plaintiff Company that the property bearing No. A-15/A/1 measuring 150 sq yds. is owned by Mr. Manoj Singhal and Sandeep Kumar Singhal and property bearing no. A-15A measuring 359.58 sq yds is owned by the Plaintiff Company M/S Chandra Associates and in these circumstances Mr. Manoj Singhal had no authority either to enter into any contract for property bearing No. A- 15A or A-15A/1.

It is further averred that in the eviction proceedings Mr Manoj Singhal gave evidence as Director of the Plaintiff Company contrary to averments made in the suit pending before Hon'ble High Court being CS(OS) No. 2075/2007 and Execution was also filed by Mr Manoj Singhal claimed himself to be the owner of the suit property. During pendency of eviction petition the defendant who was a tenant on 15 floor portion and terrace in property measuring 359.58 sq yds. raised objection of ownership of property. During pendency of proceedings the tenant/the Defendant suffered heart ailment as such decided to shift to ground floor accommodation as advised by doctors. Therefore, keeping in mind to handover possession of premises, in view of various controversies as mentioned above, the Defendant moved an application in the CS(OS) no. 2075/2007 for impleadment and for permission to deposit the key in the said suit which has been filed by a subsequent purchaser Mr. Vinod Gupta of the suit property. In said case vide order dated 11.02.2019 the Hon'ble Court was pleased to pass an order that proper forum for filing this application is the Probate Case where all the heirs of the deceased owner of the property are the parties.

It is further averred that thereafter the defendant moved an application in the said Probate case filed by the owners of the property. The said Probate Case was also not pursued by the Petitioner as such the application was also not considered. In view of the above facts to ascertain who is the real owner of the suit property the Defendant moved an application under Section 47 of CPC in Execution for determination of question to whom the keys have to be handed over. Ultimately the Defendant handed over the keys to the Ld. Executing Court on for which the defendant moved an application in 2019 during the eviction proceedings itself. The Defendant also throughout the eviction proceedings continued to deposit rent before the Id. Court. Hence in view of the above facts and submissions the present suit is not maintainable and liable to be dismissed. CONTENTIONS IN THE WRITTEN STATEMENT: On merits, it is contended that it is a settled law that ownership cannot be decided in a rent matter hence ownership of the plaintiff company was not decided or adjudicated in the rent matter. Plaintiff is not the owner of the property in question. There is no eviction order in respect of the terrace which was also a part of the tenancy but the Defendant in order to hand over the keys of the M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026 suit property to rightful owner did not contest the case. Defendant was a tenant in the premises in question since 1981. Subsequently in 1985 the Plaintiff entered into an alleged agreement to sell with the real owner. In the said sale deed a camouflage created by the Plaintiff Company by stating that Mrs. Krishna Gupta who is Bhabhi and wife of his brother/attorney is a tenant in the premises along with Jija of the real owner.

It is further contended that vide alleged sale deed dated 11.08.1986 Dr Ramesh Gupta sold 359 sq yds to M/S Chandra Associates through Manju Rani Mittal. The eviction proceedings were conducted by Mr. Manoj Singhal who was neither the Director of the Company nor owner of the suit property. He was claiming his half ownership from the alleged sale deed dated 07.07.2006 of 150 sq. yds. of property which was not part of the tenanted property. So admittedly he was not the owner of the suit property and was not entitled to take possession of the suit property. It is further contended that the possession cannot be handed over to a person who has no authority as stated by Company in CS(OS)2075/2007 which is pending for adjudication before the Hon'ble High Court by a purchaser to whom Mr. Manoj Singhal who has obtained eviction order sold the property and the Plaintiff Company in the said suit has categorically stated that the Plaintiff Company has never passed any resolution in favour of Mr. Manoj Singhal to contest case on behalf of the Plaintiff Company. The eviction decree and the judgment passed in appeal as well as Execution proceedings initiated by Mr. Manoj Singhal is non-est in the eyes of law. In order to make out a case of subletting against the JD no. 2, the DH appointed a common counsel for landlord Ramesh Gupta and for alleged tenant Krishna Gupta and her husband Tarsem to whom Ramesh Gupta gave power of attorney. Pursuant thereto filed written statement on their behalf after entering into agreement to sell by asserting that JD no. 2 is a sub tenant in the premises. Copy of written statement filed by the counsel and signed by purchaser of the premises without any authorization from the Ramesh Gupta, the alleged owner.

It is further contended that in the eviction proceedings Krishna Gupta was never served at the address where she was residing. During pendency of the case she passed away. Her LRs were never impleaded as parties. Subsequently in appeal preferred by JD no. 2 arising from some interim order, he arrayed LRs as party and JD no. 1's husband appeared and her LRs. They filed reply and denied filing any pleadings in any of the cases as alleged by the DH. Rather their case was that property is an 'HUF'. They placed on record Assessment order of Income Tax department etc. Since it is a settled law that in eviction proceedings the Court cannot adjudicate the ownership or title of the alleged owner, hence trial court did not decide the controversy who is the owner and directed the JD no. 2 to deposit rent in court. It is further contended that defendant was never asked by the Plaintiff to vacate the suit property. Defendant has never received any letter or notice for vacation of the suit property from the Plaintiff. Plaintiff straightaway filed a petition for eviction against Mrs Krishna Gupta and the defendant. Krishna Gupta was deliberately not served at the address where she was living. Even after her demise the LRs of Mrs Krishna Gupta was never impleaded as a party in eviction petition for extraneous reasons by the Plaintiff. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026

It is further contended that the case of the Plaintiff was based on falsehood and the issues raised in the eviction petition by the Defendant were not adjudicated being the eviction petition. The issues which remained adjudicated due to limitation of eviction petition and raised in preliminary objections herein above have to be adjudicated in the present suit to ascertain the facts in the interest of justice so that a litigant whose case is based on falsehood has to be thrown out with exemplary cost. Plaintiff has deliberately not placed on record the facts stated in objections. Objections were not adjudicated in view of eviction order. The Defendant himself moved an application for handing over the keys to the Hon'ble Court in view of the facts stated in the objection. Defendant did not hand over the keys to the AR of the Plaintiff but handed over the keys to the Hon'ble Court for facts stated in the objections of the Defendant.

It is further stated that the entire building was not maintained by the Plaintiff who claimed itself to be the owner of the property. The report placed on record by the Plaintiff also shows that entire building structure is in a dilapidated condition. Construction seems to be very old. It is stated in report that the building is in dilapidated condition and is danger/threat to life. For this purpose the Defendant already vide legal notice dated 19.01.2019 notified the Plaintiff to repair the building. Plaintiff was duly informed that the suit property had developed major cracks on parapet walls and floor attached to it. Plaintiff was also notified that if repairs would not be carried out, it would cause undue inconvenience to the Defendant as well as with the fall of plaster of parapet walls from the roof would cause serious accident in the nature of risk to life or injury to the Defendant, his family or to stranger also. Defendant also notified that the defendant would reserve his right to initiate appropriate legal action against the Plaintiff for inconvenience caused to the Defendant without repair.

It is further contended that defendant had maintained the suit property from inside due to his residence by spending a lot of amount on it being an old construction of 1981. Since owners of the building who were the landlord of the Defendant were not residing in the building as such the Defendant in order to maintain his residential portion of first floor had spent exorbitant amount from changing the electricity wire, drainage pipe etc. Plaintiff did not get the building ever white-washed also. Though the suit property and entire building has to be maintained by the owner of the property, but there was no owner of the property as such it was never maintained. Plaintiff is a land grabber and not owner of the suit property. It is further contended that defendant moved an application for handing over the possession of the suit property in 2017 before the Hon'ble High Court. Therefore during the pendency of the eviction proceedings which were based on falsehood the defendant himself came forward to hand over the possession to rightful owner in view of the facts stated herein above and in the said application. The Defendant moved an application before Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in a proceedings of Specific Performance of Contract filed by some Vinod Gupta against the Plaintiff and two other persons who claimed themselves to be Director of the Plaintiff Company. One of them was Manoj Singhal who had pursued the eviction petition without any authority. Therefore, in a manner the said judgment is non-est in the eyes of law. Plaintiff is not entitled to any sum of Rs. 75,000/ per month from the Defendant on account of alleged illegal occupation of the property. M/S Chandra Associates Pvt Ltd vs Arun Chopra on 27 February, 2026

Replication to the written statement was filed on behalf of plaintiff wherein the contentions raised in the written statement were controverted and the averments made in the plaint were reiterated. On the basis of pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by this Court vide order dated 11.05.2023:- Whether plaintiff is entitled to recover the suit amount as prayed for? OPP If issue no. 1 is proved in affirmative, whether plaintiff is entitled for interest thereof, if so at what rate and period? OPP. Whether there is no privity of contract between plaintiff and defendant? OPD. Whether the suit is without any cause of action? OPD. Whether the suit is not maintainable being bad for non joinder of necessary parties? OPD. Relief. EVIDENCE PROCEEDINGS: Evidence was conducted way by of three (3) successively appointed Court Commissioners in the following manner; Local Commissioners appointed. Ist LC appointed (to record PE and DE - order dated 16.04.2024). IInd LC appointed (subsequent LC - order dated 03.08.2024). IIIrd LC appointed (order dated 28.04.2025; proceedings 2025). PLAINTIFF'S EVIDENCE (PE) PW-1: Smt. Poonam Singhal AR/Director of plaintiff company. Evidence by way of affidavit EX.PW-1/A. Examination-in- chief and cross-examination recorded by LCs on: 22.07.2024 (before 1st LC, PW-1 tendered affidavit). Cross examination conducted on 2024, 10.09.2024, 14.09.2024, 05.10.2024, 19.10.2024. PW-1 was cross-examined at length on ownership, privity of contract, tenancy status, rent, condition of property, and prior proceedings (eviction, High Court CS(OS) 2075/2007, probate, etc.).
